name: matrix_feedback_creative
description: Redesign label decision rules from whole-parent confusion matrices. Both crossover and mutation may depart from the original criteria. Label identifiers, ground-truth labels and few-shot examples remain fixed; revised rules are unvalidated classification hypotheses.
both: Analyze each parent's main misclassification directions using error proportions within true-label rows, not raw counts alone; account for small row totals. First select and combine useful rules from BOTH parents, resolving conflicts by proposing a new set of decision criteria. You may add, remove, broaden, narrow or restructure conditions, evidence priorities and boundaries between labels. Do not limit crossover to concatenation or faithful paraphrase. Then mutate this unevaluated combination to explore a further useful alternative, guided by the ORIGINAL parents' matrices; no feedback has been measured for the crossover. Choose targeted or substantial changes as warranted, without requiring longer text or large edits every time. The matrices describe complete parent prompts and cannot identify causal rules or reveal unseen post content. Treat proposed causes and corrections as hypotheses; do not invent observations about posts or claim clinical validity. Keep label identifiers unchanged and examples read-only, and aim for compatibility with the supplied labeled examples. Return only the rewritten definitions, never examples or IDs. Return exactly {"crossover": VALUE, "value": VALUE}.
crossover_only: Compare BOTH parents' misclassification directions using proportions within true-label rows and their sample counts. Recombine their useful ideas into one new set of decision criteria. You may resolve conflicts, remove weak rules, introduce alternative conditions, broaden or narrow boundaries, and change evidence priorities; you need not preserve the original definitions. Perform this redesign as crossover, without a separate mutation step. Prefer concise changes that plausibly address observed confusions while retaining useful guidance; substantial rewriting is allowed but not required. Matrices describe complete parent prompts, cannot identify which component caused errors, and contain no unseen post details. Treat corrections as hypotheses, not established clinical diagnostic standards. Keep label identifiers unchanged and examples read-only, and aim for compatibility with the supplied labeled examples. Return definitions only, never examples or IDs. Return exactly {"crossover": VALUE}.
mutation_only: Use only the supplied FIRST parent's definitions and whole-prompt confusion matrix. Identify prominent error directions from proportions within true-label rows, considering their sample counts. Creatively redesign the decision criteria: you may add, delete, broaden, narrow or restructure conditions, evidence priorities and boundaries between labels. The original definitions are a starting point, not constraints to preserve. Choose a targeted revision or a substantially different rule structure according to the feedback; do not merely substitute synonyms, and do not make text longer or edits larger without a reason. Do not perform crossover. The matrix cannot establish which component caused an error or reveal the content of unseen posts. Treat causes and revisions as hypotheses, not validated clinical criteria. Keep label identifiers unchanged and examples read-only, and aim for compatibility with the supplied labeled examples. Return definitions only, never examples or IDs. Return exactly {"value": VALUE}.
